summary: Clinch Mountain, VA 100-ft steel tower on the Washington/Russell line; no longer manned, reached on foot by a gated road; NHLR-registered 2014; build date and builder not found.

facts.status_note: No longer manned (NHLR); HawkCount calls it an abandoned fire tower

access.note: Reached on foot up an old gated dirt road from Route 612 near Fugate Gap. No visitor rules or owner found in the sources read. East Coast Hiker reports the bottom steps were removed for safety.

visit.trail_note: HawkCount: about one third of a mile up the old fire tower access road. East Coast Hiker: 0.5 miles, steep, gaining 269 feet in about a quarter mile. Climbing the tower is not encouraged.

events.note: Regular fall hawkwatch counts from the tower site begin; HawkCount says coverage has continued every year since 1958
Registered September 3, 2014; nominated by Kristin Scholetzky

evidence.quote: Mendota Fire Tower sits atop Clinch Mountain, in Washington County, VA.

evidence.supports: site on the Russell and Washington County lines; HawkCount elevation 3018 ft
evidence.quote: The site is on the Russell and Washington County lines and is at an elevation of 3018 feet.
A hawkwatch has been conducted during fall migration each year since 1958 at this site.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 2,976 ft (907 m); HawkCount gives 3,018 ft for the hawkwatch site. The story reports both and does not pick one.
HawkCount says about one third of a mile; East Coast Hiker says 0.5 miles. The story reports both.

sources.title: Hike Mendota Fire Tower, Clinch Mountain in Virginia

notes_for_editor: No build date, builder, owner or staffing dates were found; the story says so. Searches returned hike guides, a Facebook post and a YouTube result. A YouTube result says the US Forest Service once maintained a tower here; that is unverified and not used. The record county 'Washington' is only one of the two counties HawkCount says the site straddles. The Register's 'no longer manned' has no date, so no staffing key is given. East Coast Hiker's note that climbing partway is possible is deliberately not used, since the tower's climbing status is not documented. Height converted from 100 ft. Two WebSearch-equivalent searches and about six page reads were used.
